bib.title: Agents: An Open-source Framework for Autonomous Language Agents

question: How can language agents with planning, memory, tools, multi-agent communication and controllable behaviour be built, customised and deployed by non-specialists through one open-source library?
hypothesis: Controlling agents with a symbolic plan (SOP) makes their behaviour more stable and predictable and easier to tune than a short task prompt alone.
contributions: Open-source AGENTS library supporting planning, long-short term memory, tool usage and web navigation, multi-agent communication with dynamic scheduling, human-agent interaction, and symbolic control via SOPs
Automated SOP generation pipeline (a meta agent) using retrieval-augmented generation
Agent Hub for sharing agents, and FastAPI deployment

method.summary: AGENTS is a Python library with three core classes (Agent, SOP, Environment) all built from one plain-text config file. An SOP is a graph of states, each holding prompt components and tool components; an LLM-based control function picks the next state and next agent. Demonstrated by case-study screenshots only.

models.name: LLM backing the agents (not named; GPT function calling is mentioned)
sentence-transformers (Reimers and Gurevych 2019) for long-term memory embeddings

inference.prompting: Prompts factorised into PromptComponents (task/goal, rules/constraints, step-by-step demonstrations, output format); config in plain text
inference.retrieval: Long-term memory: action histories embedded with sentence-transformers, stored in a VectorDB, queried by semantic search; SOP generation uses RAG

parameters.is_human: per-agent flag; True makes _act() wait for a human
parameters.dynamic scheduling: controller LLM chooses next agent from previous actions, environment and current state target; rule set in natural language in config
parameters.turn limit: none shown in Code 2 loop (while not sop.finished)

other.short-term memory: natural-language scratchpad updated by an LLM via a 'carefully tuned prompt' (prompt not given)

baselines: Table 1 feature checklist vs Transformers Agents, LangChain, Auto-GPT, Gentopia, XLang, Meta-GPT, Camel, AgentVerse
eval.protocol: No quantitative evaluation; qualitative case studies (chit-chat bot, two customer service agents, shopping assistant, sales agent, fiction studio, debate, software company, human-in-debate).

results.claim: The paper reports no benchmark or ablation; evidence is case-study screenshots only.
results.setup: System description of the AGENTS library (v3, Dec 2023); no experiments, qualitative case studies only.
results.quote: We then present a few case studies on different language agents built with the library, including single-agent systems, multi-agent systems, and systems that require human-agent interaction.

results.claim: Self-scored feature checklist: AGENTS is claimed the only framework supporting tool usage, long-short memory and multi-agent at once.
results.setup: Table 1, 9 frameworks x 5 binary columns, no criteria or versions given
results.quote: We can see that AGENTS is the only framework that supports tool usage, long-short term memory, and multi-agent communication at the same time.
results.note: Table 1 itself ticks tool usage, memory, multi-agent and human-agent for AgentVerse, so the sentence contradicts the table; only symbolic control is unique to AGENTS.

results.claim: SOP symbolic plans are claimed to make behaviour more stable/predictable and easier to tune; not measured.
results.quote: making agents' behavior more stable/predictable and facilitating tuning/optimizing agents at the same time

results.claim: Existing frameworks that depend on a short task description are said to give run-to-run inconsistency; asserted without data.
results.quote: This results in significant randomness and inconsistency across different runs

results.claim: Dynamic scheduling lets an LLM controller pick the next acting agent instead of fixed order.
results.quote: AGENTS includes a controller function that dynamically decides which agent will perform the next action using an LLM

results.claim: Human-in-the-loop is a per-agent flag where a human plays an agent role, not a pause/approval mechanism.
results.quote: we include a “_is_human” property to an agent.

results.claim: The core run loop is a few lines with no turn limit.

limits: No quantitative evaluation, ablation, user study, cost or latency
Feature table is self-assessed; text and table disagree on AgentVerse
Automatic SOP generation details deferred to an unpublished paper (Zhou et al. 2023b, 'To be published')
Frameworks compared are 2023 versions; field has moved on
Models used in case studies are not named

terms.definition: An SOP is a graph of multiple states that defines different situations an agent may encounter while accomplishing a task, and the transition rules between the states.
an option to define a controller agent that acts as a “moderator” and decides which agent to perform the next action considering their roles and the current history

lineage.quote: AGENTS integrates the memory components in [Zhou et al., 2023a]
